## Verdict
- Answer: One Prism table call returned usable figures for 4 of 6 cancer types, but they are not comparable response rates. Each comes from a different measure, population and study design. [c1]
- Decision: Treat this as a map of what the corpus states, not a ranking. Do not choose between cancer types on these figures. Use disease-specific pivotal trials or meta-analyses for that.
- Confidence: low - six rows, 3 to 5 papers each, a single abstract-level extraction per row, and heterogeneous measures. [c1]
- What would change it: Retrieving trial-level ORR with a common definition (PD-1/PD-L1 monotherapy, RECIST 1.1) for each cancer type.

## What the data shows
Rows answered: 4 of 6 [c1]. Window: no date window was set on the call [c1].

- **Melanoma:** 32.4% partial or complete response (93 of 287 patients on pembrolizumab) [c1]. This is an imaging-analysis study (2022, JAMA Oncology, trial tier) and not a pivotal efficacy trial. 3 papers [c1].
- **Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC):** The ORR risk ratio is 0.80 (95% CI 0.74 to 0.88) for adding a checkpoint inhibitor to chemotherapy plus anti-angiogenic therapy (C/A) after EGFR-TKI resistance [c1]. It is a ratio, not a response rate. PFS HR was 0.67 and OS HR 0.89 [c1]. Source: a 2025 meta-analysis of eight randomized trials. 3 papers [c1]. The abstract quote gives RR 0.80 with the checkpoint inhibitor arm favored; I am not reading its direction beyond what the abstract says (see limits).
- **Renal cell carcinoma:** null. 4 papers address the topic, but none states a matching figure in its abstract [c1].
- **Bladder (urothelial) cancer:** 44.4% ORR in arm B and 0% in arm A of a phase 1 trial of pembrolizumab with sequential vs concomitant stereotactic body radiotherapy (2019, trial). The arms are small and the setting is combination therapy [c1]. 4 papers [c1].
- **Colorectal cancer:** 55.6% response per RECIST 1.1 at month 2 in Latino patients, with a difference between ethnicities (p = 0.048) [c1]. This is a subgroup in a radiomics study (2023). It is not an immunotherapy response rate for colorectal cancer overall, and the abstract does not say the treatment was immunotherapy. 5 papers [c1].
- **Breast cancer:** null. The corpus returned was news (6 articles), and none states a figure. The top item was a 2026-05-31 investor-conference item on a KAT6 inhibitor [c1].

## Comparison
No valid common scale exists. The 32.4% (melanoma), 44.4% (bladder arm B) and 55.6% (colorectal subgroup) are proportions, but they differ in treatment, line of therapy, population and sample. The NSCLC 0.80 is a relative measure. A ratio or delta between rows would therefore be misleading, and I do not compute one. The only like-for-like delta available is within the bladder row: 44.4% vs 0% between arms A and B [c1].

## Evidence
- [r1] Early Readout on Overall Survival of Patients With Melanoma Treated With Immunotherapy Using a Novel Imaging Analysis. JAMA Oncology, 2022, trial tier. doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2021.6818. Supports: 93 of 287 (32.4%) partial or complete response. Quote: "partial or complete response (93 of 287 [32.4%]), stable disease (90 of 287 [31.3%]), or progressive disease (104 of 287 [36.2%])." [c1]
- [r2] Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in EGFR-TKI-Resistant Chemotherapy-Naïve Advanced NSCLC: A Meta-Analysis Based on Eight Randomized Trials. JCO Precision Oncology, 2025, meta-analysis tier. doi:10.1200/PO-24-00907. Supports: ORR RR 0.80. Quote: "ORR (RR, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.74 to 0.88]; P < .001)". [c1]
- [r3] Age-Related Survival Disparities in Advanced Renal Carcinoma in the ICI Era using SEER and Meta-analysis. Scientific Reports, 2025, meta-analysis tier. doi:10.1038/s41598-025-06297-y. Supports only that RCC papers exist; no figure. [c1]
- [r4] Randomized Phase 1 Trial of Pembrolizumab with Sequential Versus Concomitant SBRT in Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma. European Urology, 2019, trial tier. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2019.01.009. Quote: "Overall response rates of 0% and 44.4% were noted in arms A and B". [c1]
- [r5] Ethnic diversity in treatment response for colorectal cancer: proof of concept for radiomics-driven enrichment trials. European Radiology, 2023, trial tier. doi:10.1007/s00330-023-09862-z. Quote: "higher response rate (55.6%) in Latinos." [c1]
- News: 2026-05-31, investor-conference item on Olema Pharmaceuticals, strength very_low. No figure. [c1]

- Window: the call set no date window. The cited papers run 2019 to 2025 and the one news item is 2026-05-31, which is 145 days before 2026-10-23.

## What the data shows
Each ORR below is my recollection of a named trial, so every value is tagged [rN] (est.): the trial is the claimed source, and the number has not been re-checked. Rates are not directly comparable. The trials differ in line of therapy, in single-agent versus combination regimens, and in biomarker selection (PD-L1, MSI).

- **Highest response:** classical Hodgkin lymphoma ~69% [r6] (est.) after prior therapy. Pembrolizumab in Merkel cell carcinoma ~56% [r16] (est.). Cemiplimab in advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma ~47% [r11] (est.). Nivolumab plus ipilimumab in melanoma ~58% [r1] (est.).
- **Biomarker-defined:** MSI-H/dMMR colorectal cancer on first-line pembrolizumab ~44% [r7] (est.), and across MSI-H tumors of many types ~34% [r9] (est.). MSS colorectal cancer responds at roughly 0–5% (est.).
- **Mid-range:** renal cell carcinoma with nivolumab plus ipilimumab ~42% [r3] (est.). Mesothelioma with nivolumab plus ipilimumab ~40% [r10] (est.). Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with PD-L1 ≥50% on first-line pembrolizumab ~45% [r2] (est.). Hepatocellular carcinoma with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab ~30% [r8] (est.).
- **Low:** second-line urothelial carcinoma ~21% [r4] (est.). Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma on pembrolizumab alone ~17% [r5] (est.). Gastric cancer, third-line ~12% [r14] (est.). Triple-negative breast cancer on pembrolizumab monotherapy ~12% [r15] (est.). Ovarian cancer ~8% [r13] (est.). Castration-resistant prostate cancer ~5% [r12] (est.).
- **Near zero:** glioblastoma showed no survival benefit with nivolumab [r17] (est.). Microsatellite-stable pancreatic cancer has essentially no responses (est.).

## Method and limits
- **Windows:** the trials date from roughly 2015 to 2022. My knowledge cutoff is June 2026, so about 4 months separate it from today (2026-10-23), and anything published since is not covered.
- **Lanes:** I used only my own knowledge. No Prism calls, searches or document retrieval were run.
- **Coverage:** one headline trial per tumor type, not a systematic review. Many tumor types are missing, including SCLC, cervical, endometrial, esophageal, and the non-Hodgkin lymphomas.
- **Censoring and match mode:** no search was run, so neither applies.
- **What the numbers are:** approximate ORRs recalled per trial. They are not pooled estimates, and they carry no confidence intervals.
- **What they are not:** comparable across rows. Line of therapy, regimen, biomarker selection and ORR criteria differ between trials. ORR also does not equal survival benefit, as durable responses and survival gains can differ from ORR.
- **Interpretation:** the "baseline" in the Comparison is my choice, and the grouping into high, mid, low and near-zero bands is my reading.
- **What the data cannot answer:** any ORR for the tumor types not listed, current post-2022 values, and any exact value for MSS colorectal or pancreatic cancer.
